newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe tobacco output seen 14 percent up in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe tobacco output seen 14 percent up in 1998.

text.p: Zimbabwe, the world's fourth largest flue-cured tobacco producer, plans to boost output by 14 percent in 1998, assuming normal weather conditions, a top industry official said on Wednesday.
Zimbabwe Tobacco Association (ZTA) president Robert Webb said it was crucial for Zimbabwe, the world's second largest exporter of the yellow leaf after Brazil, to maintain its world market share.
"After extensive consultation with merchants and customers abroad a production level of 245 million kilograms would be acceptable for the 1997/98 season," Rob Webb told an annual ZTA congress.
"With the supply and demand of tobacco coming into balance, we should adhere to the policy of not overproducing," he said.

"However, with the past wet season and the impact of reduced yields from a crop of 91,000 hectares and, in assuming normal weather conditions prevail in 1998, it is crucial that we maintain our position of world market share," he added.
Zimbabwe was looking at producing a record crop of 260 million kg this year but waterlogging cut output by almost 30 percent to 214 million kg.
The southern African country is the world's fourth largest producer of tobacco after China, the U.S. and Brazil, and the second largest exporter after Brazil. China uses up all its crop.
